newsitem.title: CHILE: No small talk, sideburns, Pinochet tells officers.
newsitem.headline: No small talk, sideburns, Pinochet tells officers.

text.p: Former Chilean dictator Gen. Augusto Pinochet told officers on Thursday that they should avoid gossiping about the military, watch their drink and not wear sideburns.

"When you are in embassies and they talk about the army you must leave the conversation immediately as there are people who say whatever they like about your commander-in-chief," Pinochet, who continues to serve as army chief, told officers at a ceremony to award emblems to 70 unit commanders.
"You must explain clearly that you are leaving because of the nonsense they are talking," the 81-year old general, known for his outspoken comments, said.

He said military officials and their families also must make sure to keep up their appearances in Chile or abroad. "You mustn't wear sideburns in the centre of London. You must also take great care of your wife and children," he said.
"All this is very important for the army ... I've had to tell people off for their poor appearance."
He also said officers must avoid drinking too much in case they become indiscreet.
Pinochet, one of the world's longest-serving army officers, ruled Chile from 1973 to 1990 after a bloody military coup in which Marxist President Salvador Allende was overthrown and killed.
